text:
Los Angeles keeps losing games it controls. Saturday's 5-2 loss to Pittsburgh was the purest version: the Kings outshot the Penguins badly and still lost by three. At 5-8-2, our race model says the Kings have left 4.6 points on the table compared with what their play deserved.

The process isn't dominant, though. LA takes 51 percent of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), and its goalies have allowed about six more goals than the chances against them should produce. That second number is the real story. Fix the saves and this is a playoff team; our simulations give them 41 percent as it stands.

The good news has a name. Brandt Clarke is having the breakout everyone waited for, playing in a "leadership role" per NHL.com, and his pair with Erik Gustafsson takes 62 percent of the expected goals. Adrian Kempe passed Dustin Brown on the franchise list with a hat trick against San Jose, and the Kempe, Artemi Panarin and Alex Laferriere line has outscored teams 8-1. Quinton Byfield's name has popped up in trade chatter, which is the kind of thing that happens to young players on teams that are losing. We'd be patient.
headline: The Kings are better than 5-8-2, but not by enough yet
